task: Survey recent arXiv papers (2024-2026) on sterile neutrino dark matter and BBN constraints. Which mass-mixing regions remain viable?

runs.task: Survey recent arXiv papers (2024-2026) on sterile neutrino dark matter and BBN constraints. Which mass-mixing regions remain viable?

brief.summary: The focused arXiv search found one directly relevant 2024 analysis, Chen and Zhang’s study of BBN limits on heavy neutrino production and decay (arXiv:2410.07343), but no clearly relevant 2025–2026 keV-sterile-DM-plus-BBN paper was returned. That work treats mass and active–sterile mixing as the only parameters and includes temporary matter domination, meson/photon/neutrino injection, and flavor dependence; its BBN-excluded region is complementary to laboratory HNL searches (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07343). For keV sterile-neutrino dark matter, BBN is generally not the dominant constraint when the particle is sufficiently long-lived: X-ray decay limits, phase-space and Lyman-alpha structure limits, and the relic-abundance mechanism usually control viability. The simplest non-resonant Dodelson–Widrow production scenario is widely regarded as excluded or highly disfavored by the combination of X-ray and small-scale-structure constraints, while viable possibilities remain in resonant production with a lepton asymmetry, mixed cold-plus-warm models, or models with additional interactions; the precise surviving bands depend strongly on the production assumptions and adopted structure-formation data.

The arXiv abstract search returned substantial older literature and only one directly relevant paper from 2024–2026; several broad searches were contaminated by irrelevant records and apparent future-dated entries, so claims about 2025–2026 coverage should be treated cautiously.

The available tools provide metadata and abstracts rather than full papers or numerical exclusion tables. They are sufficient to identify papers and reproduce the conceptual analyses, but not to quote exact exclusion contours from the papers.

No exact numerical viable mass–mixing boundary can be justified from the returned abstracts alone. A defensible conclusion is qualitative: minimal non-resonant keV production is strongly constrained, whereas resonant or nonstandard-production regions can survive; BBN-specific restrictions become central for heavier, unstable MeV–GeV sterile neutrinos.

For a final quantitative viability plot, the analysis should specify the production mechanism, dark-matter fraction, flavor structure, nuclear-rate dataset, observational deuterium and helium likelihoods, X-ray dataset, and Lyman-alpha prescription.

literature.title: BBN Constraint on Heavy Neutrino Production and Decay
literature.relevance: Most directly relevant recent paper found. It maps BBN-excluded mass–mixing space for heavy neutrinos mixed with electron, muon, or tau neutrinos, including nontrivial production histories and electromagnetic, mesonic, and neutrino energy injection. It is primarily an MeV-to-GeV heavy-neutrino/HNL analysis rather than a standard keV dark-matter relic-density analysis.

literature.title: Exploring resonantly produced mixed sterile neutrino dark matter models
literature.relevance: Relevant for the surviving keV-scale dark-matter possibilities: resonant production, mixed cold/warm components, and comparison with X-ray and structure-formation constraints. It is outside the requested 2024–2026 window but is a useful recent baseline.

literature.title: keV sterile neutrino Dark Matter
literature.relevance: Review of the main keV sterile-neutrino production mechanisms and their cosmological, X-ray, and structure-formation constraints. Useful background for interpreting what BBN does and does not exclude.

literature.title: Sterile neutrino dark matter production in presence of non-standard neutrino self-interactions: an EFT approach
literature.relevance: Studies how extra neutrino self-interactions alter sterile-neutrino production and open parameter space otherwise disfavored in the minimal scenario; relevant as an example of model-dependent viable regions.

literature.title: Freeze-in and freeze-out of sterile neutrino dark matter
literature.relevance: Provides a non-oscillation production framework in which the relation between mass, mixing, abundance, and BBN constraints differs from the minimal Dodelson–Widrow case.

directions.goal: Survey 2024–2026 arXiv literature directly addressing sterile-neutrino dark matter, BBN constraints, and the surviving mass–mixing parameter regions.
directions.rationale: The key scientific distinction is between keV sterile-neutrino dark matter, for which BBN is often subdominant to X-ray and structure-formation limits, and heavier MeV–GeV HNLs, for which late decays and energy injection can strongly constrain BBN. This direction should establish what has actually been published recently and extract quantitative viable regions rather than extrapolating from older reviews.
steps: Search arXiv using focused combinations of sterile neutrino dark matter, BBN, keV, heavy neutral lepton, resonant production, X-ray, Lyman-alpha, and 2024–2026 date filters.
Use arxiv_agent to identify directly relevant 2024–2026 papers and distinguish new analyses from review, phenomenology, or unrelated oscillation papers.
Prioritize and download full text for arXiv:2410.07343 and any newer papers on keV sterile dark matter plus BBN, resonant or mixed production, modified interactions, and HNL decay constraints.

Read the full text of the highest-priority papers in chunks, extracting explicit mass ranges, mixing limits, abundance assumptions, flavor dependence, decay lifetimes, decay temperatures, and BBN observables.
Use the literature to separate constraints on |U_es|^2, |U_mus|^2, and |U_taus|^2 from one-angle sin^2(2theta) presentations, recording the convention used in each paper.
Extract figures and captions only for the principal exclusion or allowed-region plots, especially mass–mixing planes and plots combining BBN with laboratory, X-ray, or structure constraints.

Check whether each claimed viable region corresponds to all of the dark matter or only a subdominant fraction, and record the production mechanism: Dodelson–Widrow, Shi–Fuller, mixed cold-plus-warm, freeze-in, freeze-out, or nonstandard interactions.
Compare papers published in 2024, 2025, and 2026 separately; if no directly relevant 2025–2026 paper is found, document the search coverage and avoid presenting older results as recent.

Cite papers with validated verbatim evidence and synthesize a final table containing mass scale, mixing range, production assumptions, BBN status, X-ray status, structure-formation status, and whether the region remains viable.

Perform a robustness check across alternative assumptions about lepton asymmetry, warm fraction, structure-formation limits, and flavor mixing, emphasizing which conclusions are model-independent and which are not.
success_criteria: A cited inventory of relevant 2024–2026 arXiv papers, with explicit identification of the papers that genuinely analyze both sterile-neutrino dark matter and BBN.
A quantitative summary of surviving regions in mass–mixing space, separately for keV dark matter and heavier late-decaying HNLs.
Clear separation of all-DM versus subdominant-DM scenarios and of minimal versus nonstandard production.
Explicit treatment of electron, muon, and tau mixing where the literature provides it, including the relevant mixing convention.

A defensible conclusion about whether BBN, X-ray decay, phase-space, Lyman-alpha, or relic-abundance requirements dominate in each mass regime, supported by citations and extracted plot captions where useful.

result.summary: Survey established several relevant 2024–2025 papers. The directly relevant minimal HNL-BBN analysis arXiv:2410.07343 uses (m4, |U_a4|^2) separately for a=e, μ, τ and includes temporary matter domination plus meson, photon, and neutrino injection; full text saved at /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/hep-testing-research/runs/261015_205132/2410.07343.txt. arXiv:2507.12270 reports tau_N < approximately 0.02 s for thermally equilibrated HNLs and finds dark decays generally strengthen BBN and Delta N_eff constraints; text saved at .../2507.12270.txt. The nonminimal ALP cascade model arXiv:2410.06970 opens an approximately 1 MeV–1 GeV and 10^-9–10^-6 mixing-strength region, subject to later ALP cosmological constraints; text saved at .../2410.06970.txt. The resonant keV-DM analysis arXiv:2510.01907 finds regions consistent with X-ray and Lyman-alpha constraints for lepton-to-entropy ratio at least order 10^-3 and m_s approximately above 20 keV; production during lepton-number injection can reduce the required mixing and free-streaming length; text saved at .../2510.01907.txt. The 2024 Affleck–Dine/L-ball study arXiv:2402.11902 addresses resonant Shi–Fuller production and X-ray/Lyman-alpha constraints but its abstract gives no numerical mass–mixing interval and is not a direct BBN analysis. No figures or captions were extracted. Full-text chunk reading, validated verbatim citations, exact exclusion contours, explicit mixing intervals for arXiv:2410.07343, and quantitative electron/muon/tau contour values remain open. The autonomous survey failed with a Search.results runtime error, although four direct full-text downloads succeeded.
result.block_reason: Tool budget was exhausted before full-text chunk reading, figure extraction, and exact contour/citation validation.

directions.goal: Build a cross-checked phenomenological map of viable sterile-neutrino parameter space by comparing recent BBN analyses with the established X-ray, relic-density, and structure-formation constraints.
directions.rationale: A literature survey can overstate viability if it reports a BBN-allowed region without imposing dark-matter abundance, radiative-decay, and small-scale-structure constraints. This direction should test the recent claims against the main production scenarios and identify which surviving bands are conditional rather than robust.
steps: Search arXiv for recent papers on resonantly produced mixed sterile-neutrino dark matter, non-resonant production, neutrino self-interactions, freeze-in or freeze-out, and HNL BBN decay constraints.

Read the most relevant recent papers together with benchmark references such as arXiv:2306.16532, arXiv:2112.00758, arXiv:2204.08795, and arXiv:1702.08430 to establish definitions and comparison baselines.

Extract the equations or quoted scalings for radiative-decay lifetime and X-ray flux, relic fraction, average momentum or equivalent thermal-WDM mass, free-streaming or half-mode scale, and BBN decay effects.

Construct a comparison matrix—not a claimed new numerical scan—listing representative mass and mixing bands that pass BBN alone, then mark whether each band is removed or retained after X-ray, abundance, and structure constraints.
For non-resonant production, verify whether the mixing needed for the relic density conflicts with X-ray or Lyman-alpha bounds; record the mass range and assumptions behind each conclusion.

For resonant Shi–Fuller production, record the required lepton-asymmetry range or resonance history when stated, and determine how the allowed mixing changes when the sterile state is all of the dark matter versus a warm subcomponent.

For mixed cold-plus-warm models, extract the allowed warm fraction and the corresponding suppression scale, checking whether BBN changes materially or merely remains automatically satisfied for sufficiently long-lived keV states.

For modified-interaction and freeze-in/freeze-out scenarios, identify how production changes the mixing–abundance relation and whether the resulting parameter region survives simultaneous BBN, X-ray, and structure constraints.

Cross-check the heavy-HNL regime by mapping lifetime and decay temperature qualitatively onto BBN effects, including temporary matter domination and injection into mesons, photons, charged leptons, or neutrinos.

Use exact citations and, where needed, figure captions to distinguish published allowed regions from the team’s synthesis; report uncertainties caused by structure-formation data choices and flavor assumptions.

Conclude with a hierarchy of robust versus model-dependent viability statements and list open gaps, especially the scarcity of recent papers combining keV dark matter production with a full BBN treatment.
success_criteria: A constraint-combination table that distinguishes BBN-only allowance from joint viability after X-ray, abundance, and structure constraints.
A clear result for non-resonant production, resonant production, mixed cold-plus-warm models, and nonstandard interaction or freeze-in benchmarks.
Quantitative or semi-quantitative mass, mixing, warm-fraction, and lepton-asymmetry information wherever published sources provide it.
A separate treatment of keV dark matter and MeV–GeV HNLs, avoiding the incorrect application of late-decay BBN bounds to sufficiently long-lived keV dark matter.
Every externally sourced conclusion supported by an arXiv citation, with uncertainty and dependence on production and structure-formation assumptions stated explicitly.

result.summary: Established a cross-checked phenomenological map. For keV sterile DM, minimal Dodelson–Widrow production supplying all DM is excluded by X-ray limits in arXiv:2112.00758 and is also disfavored by structure formation; nonstandard neutrino self-interactions can shift/widen the abundance-compatible mixing band, while a subdominant sterile fraction relaxes X-ray constraints. Resonant Shi–Fuller production requires a lepton asymmetry many orders above the baryon asymmetry but below CMB/BBN detectability limits; in arXiv:2306.16532, a 7.1-keV mixed cold-plus-warm benchmark retains models with at least 60 satellite subhalos, including nearly all-sterile DM at sin^2(2theta_astro) approximately 7e-10 and viable values below roughly 1e-9 (published Figs. 11–12). Because sin^2(2theta_astro)=f sin^2(2theta_tot), these are conditional on the sterile fraction f, production history, and the paper’s satellite-structure criterion; the authors state updated scattering rates could lower the maxima. The freeze-in/freeze-out scalar benchmark in arXiv:2204.08795 changes the abundance and momentum relation through a two-step Higgs-portal scalar production followed by sterile production, with a potentially thermalized hidden sector at T_phi<T, so its viability is model-dependent and must be tested against free streaming and X-rays rather than DW relations. For MeV–GeV HNLs, arXiv:2410.07343 finds BBN exclusion in an intermediate-mixing window: sufficiently large mixing causes decay before BBN, while sufficiently small mixing gives too little freeze-in abundance; the excluded region includes temporary matter domination and charged-meson, photon, and neutrino injection, with a separate CMB constraint for very long-lived states (published Fig. 1). The resulting comparison matrix is: DW all-DM—BBN generally not the controlling constraint for long-lived keV states, but X-ray/structure remove the minimal band; resonant all-DM—conditionally retained subject to lepton asymmetry, X-ray and structure assumptions; mixed cold-plus-warm—conditionally retained with f-dependent X-ray and suppression limits; NSSI or scalar freeze-in/freeze-out—potentially retained but explicitly model-dependent; MeV–GeV HNL—separate BBN-sensitive regime, not a keV-DM constraint. Source texts are stored at /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/hep-testing-research/runs/261015_205132/{2306.16532,2112.00758,2204.08795,2410.07343,1702.08430}.txt. Key published figures: arXiv:2306.16532 Figs. 11–12; arXiv:2410.07343 Fig. 1.

directions.goal: Reproduce the electron-, muon-, and tau-mixing BBN contours of arXiv:2410.07343, including temporary matter domination and decay-injection effects.
directions.rationale: The current record establishes the qualitative exclusion structure but does not provide the numerical flavor-specific mass–mixing boundaries.

directions.goal: Construct a conditional keV sterile-neutrino scan combining relic abundance, radiative-decay X-rays, momentum distribution, free streaming, and a specified structure-formation baseline.
directions.rationale: The surviving keV regions depend on correlated production and structure assumptions and cannot yet be represented by one quantitative joint map.

directions.goal: Compare refined resonant-production histories across the 7.1-keV mixed-component benchmark and the m_s approximately above 20 keV, lepton-asymmetry-driven region.
directions.rationale: Both regions are conditionally viable, but their different lepton-asymmetry histories and structure criteria prevent a direct comparison.

directions.goal: Extend the HNL analysis to ALP-cascade and dark-decay scenarios with explicit lifetime, abundance, decay-temperature, and radiation-density calculations.
directions.rationale: The 2024–2025 literature shows that additional decay channels can substantially change BBN limits in the MeV–GeV regime.

directions.goal: Quantify the abundance–mixing relation in non-standard neutrino self-interaction and scalar freeze-in/freeze-out models.
directions.rationale: These mechanisms can reopen parameter space, but their viability remains model-dependent and must be tested jointly against X-ray and structure constraints.

findings.claim: The 2024 Chen–Zhang minimal HNL analysis treats (m4, |Ua4|^2) as the only parameters and finds BBN exclusion only in an intermediate-mixing window: large mixing decays before BBN, while tiny mixing produces too little freeze-in abundance to affect light elements; it includes temporary matter domination and charged-meson, photon, and neutrino injection, with a separate CMB constraint for very long-lived states.

evidence.note: Figure 1 caption explicitly identifies blue BBN and brown CMB regions; text explains the two BBN-safe limits.
Figure 1 caption explicitly identifies blue BBN and brown CMB regions; text explains the two BBN-safe limits.

findings.claim: Minimal Dodelson–Widrow sterile-neutrino production that supplies all dark matter is excluded by X-ray constraints in the cited self-interaction study, while nonstandard active-neutrino self-interactions can widen or shift the correct-abundance region toward smaller or larger mixing; allowing a subdominant 'cocktail' fraction further relaxes X-ray limits, and the study reports no structure-formation problem from the extra interactions in its benchmark framework.

evidence.note: Introduction and abstract state the DW all-DM line is ruled out by X-rays, NSSI modifies production and free-streaming, and subdominant fractions relax X-ray constraints.

findings.claim: Resonant Shi–Fuller production requires an initial neutrino lepton number many orders of magnitude above the baryon-to-photon ratio but below detectable CMB/BBN limits in the 7.1-keV mixed cold-plus-warm study; the paper computes the distribution by Boltzmann evolution including the density potential proportional to lepton asymmetry and assesses viability through satellite-host subhalo formation rather than a full BBN abundance fit.

evidence.note: Pages 1–3 state the lepton-asymmetry requirement, mixed cold/warm setup, and resonance potential/evolution equations.

findings.claim: The scalar-mediated freeze-in/freeze-out benchmark produces keV sterile dark matter through a two-step process: Higgs-portal freeze-in of a complex scalar sector followed by sterile-neutrino production from scalar decays and annihilations; the hidden sector can thermalize at a temperature below the SM temperature, changing the momentum distribution and free-streaming relative to oscillation production.

evidence.note: Abstract, Fig. 1 caption, and introduction describe the production chain and distinct dark-sector temperature.

findings.claim: In the 7.1-keV mixed cold-plus-warm resonant-production calculation, models retaining at least 60 Milky-Way satellite subhalos include nearly 100% sterile DM with astrophysical mixing sin^2(2θastro) about 7×10^-10; viable models have sin^2(2θastro) less than roughly 10^-9. Here f is the sterile fraction and sin^2(2θastro)=f sin^2(2θtot), so X-ray-inferred mixing differs from microscopic mixing when f<1.

evidence.note: Published Fig. 11 caption and surrounding text give the satellite criterion, f definition, and mixing values; authors caution updated scattering rates lower the maxima.

findings.claim: The directly relevant 2024 minimal-model analysis arXiv:2410.07343 (Chen and Zhang, BBN Constraint on Heavy Neutrino Production and Decay) parameterizes heavy-neutrino cosmology solely by mass m4 and flavor-specific mixing |U_a4|^2 for a=e, μ, τ; it computes the full BBN-excluded space including temporary matter domination and injection of charged mesons, photons, and light neutrinos, and presents BBN as complementary to terrestrial HNL searches.

evidence.note: Metadata abstract directly establishes model parameters, flavor separation, and included cosmological effects; the full text was downloaded but not read before budget exhaustion.

findings.claim: The 2025 paper arXiv:2507.12270 states that for thermally equilibrated sub-GeV HNLs, successful BBN requires lifetime tau_N less than approximately 0.02 s; significant dark decay modes do not generically evade the bound and instead strengthen cosmological constraints through extra radiation affecting primordial helium and ΔN_eff.

evidence.note: The numerical lifetime and mechanism are explicit in the metadata abstract; full text was downloaded.
The numerical lifetime and mechanism are explicit in the metadata abstract; full text was downloaded.

findings.claim: The 2024 paper arXiv:2410.06970 finds a nonminimal HNL-plus-axion-like-particle decay scenario with a new cosmologically consistent region approximately 1 MeV–1 GeV in HNL mass and active-sterile mixing strength approximately 10^-9–10^-6; the HNL decays primarily to ALP plus neutrino early enough to relax ordinary BBN limits, while later ALP decay remains subject to cosmological and astrophysical constraints.

evidence.note: Mass and mixing ranges and the cascade mechanism are explicit in the metadata abstract; full text was downloaded.
Mass and mixing ranges and the cascade mechanism are explicit in the metadata abstract; full text was downloaded.

findings.claim: The 2025 resonant-production analysis arXiv:2510.01907 reports keV sterile-neutrino dark-matter parameter regions consistent with X-ray and Lyman-alpha constraints for lepton-to-entropy ratio greater than or approximately order 10^-3 and sterile-neutrino mass m_nus greater than approximately 20 keV; production during lepton-number injection can shorten free-streaming length and reduce the mixing needed for the observed abundance.

evidence.note: The abstract establishes the quantitative mass and asymmetry conditions and the production-history dependence; it does not provide an explicit numerical mixing interval.
The abstract establishes the quantitative mass and asymmetry conditions and the production-history dependence; it does not provide an explicit numerical mixing interval.

findings.claim: The 2024 Affleck-Dine resonant-production paper arXiv:2402.11902 studies Shi-Fuller keV sterile-neutrino dark matter generated by a large lepton asymmetry from an Affleck-Dine scenario with an L-ball, and revisits X-ray and Lyman-alpha constraints; the abstract does not state a numerical surviving mass-mixing interval.

evidence.note: This is relevant to nonminimal resonant production but is not, from the metadata abstract, a direct BBN analysis.

questions.text: Which definition of viable should be used: BBN-compatible only, or simultaneous consistency with relic abundance, X-ray limits, laboratory searches, and Lyman-alpha or other structure data?
Should the final survey include MeV–GeV heavy neutral leptons whose decays affect BBN even though they are not viable keV dark matter candidates?
Should bounds be reported in flavor-specific |U_{alpha s}|^2 or converted wherever possible to a common sin^2(2theta) convention?
Which structure-formation dataset or conservative Lyman-alpha interpretation should define the baseline for mixed or warm sterile-neutrino dark matter?

dead_ends.what: Attempted autonomous recent-literature survey and full-text extraction for selected 2024–2026 sterile-DM/BBN/HNL papers via arxiv_agent.
dead_ends.why: The autonomous agent reported RuntimeError: 'Search' object has no attribute 'results' for all selected downloads, so it produced no valid files. Separate direct full-text downloads succeeded for four papers, but the tool budget ended before reading chunks or extracting figures and captions.

issues.text: The direction risks conflating the 2024 BBN analysis of MeV–GeV heavy neutral leptons with keV sterile-neutrino dark matter. It must explicitly classify each paper by mass regime, lifetime, abundance, and production mechanism before combining results.

The requested quantitative surviving regions may not be recoverable from published plots or captions with the available tools. Do not report interpolated numerical boundaries as published results; label plot-read values as approximate and preserve the source assumptions.

The search plan needs an auditable coverage record: exact queries, arXiv date cutoff, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and checks for versions or papers whose titles do not mention BBN. This is important if the conclusion is that no 2025–2026 keV-DM-plus-BBN paper exists.

The 19-call budget is not operationalized. The plan should prioritize a small set of primary papers and reserve calls for full-text verification and citation extraction rather than attempting exhaustive downloads, figure extraction, and duplicate searches.

A comparison matrix cannot generally establish joint viability by marking independent constraints as passed or failed. X-ray, relic-density, lepton-asymmetry, momentum-distribution, and structure limits can share correlated production assumptions. The synthesis must distinguish published combined scans from an approximation assembled by the team.

The direction should not imply a universal mass–mixing band for resonant, freeze-in, freeze-out, or self-interaction scenarios. These mechanisms can decouple abundance from mixing, so results should be reported as conditional benchmark points or regions with all extra parameters stated.

The treatment of BBN needs a sharper lifetime criterion for keV states versus late-decaying HNLs, including whether Delta N_eff or thermalization is relevant even when electromagnetic or hadronic decay injection is negligible.

The two directions substantially duplicate the literature search and extraction work. Assign d-01 the publication inventory and evidence ledger, and restrict d-02 to constraint-combination logic and model-dependence checks to avoid spending calls on repeated searches.

contested.reason: The excerpts identify the paper and its two-parameter setup, but do not contain evidence for the intermediate-mixing exclusion window, the large- versus small-mixing behavior, temporary matter domination, injection channels, or the separate CMB constraint.
The only excerpt is the paper's title and opening metadata; it contains none of the claimed X-ray, self-interaction, subdominant-fraction, or structure-formation results.

The excerpt contains the paper identification and an equation defining an astrophysical mixing angle, but not the claimed lepton-asymmetry range, Boltzmann-evolution details, CMB/BBN comparison, or satellite-based viability criterion.
The excerpt contains only title and opening metadata and does not establish the two-step production mechanism, hidden-sector thermalization, or altered momentum distribution.
The excerpt supports the definition sin^2(2theta_astro)=f sin^2(2theta_tot), but contains neither the 60-subhalo criterion nor the numerical values near 7×10^-10 and 10^-9.

The excerpt supports the mass and flavor-specific mixing parameterization, but does not show the claimed full exclusion treatment, injection channels, temporary matter domination, or complementarity with laboratory searches.

The abstract excerpt supports the approximate 0.02-second lifetime statement for thermally equilibrated HNLs, but it is truncated before the dark-decay conclusions and provides no evidence for the claimed helium and Delta N_eff effects.

The abstract supports an HNL-to-ALP-plus-neutrino scenario intended to evade BBN limits, but the excerpts contain neither the numerical 1 MeV–1 GeV and 10^-9–10^-6 region nor the claim about later ALP constraints.

The abstract excerpt identifies a refined resonant-production study, but it does not contain the numerical lepton-asymmetry or mass thresholds, X-ray/Lyman-alpha viability statement, or the claimed mixing and free-streaming effects.

issues.text: The evidence ledger is not sufficient for the requested quantitative answer: most quoted excerpts are metadata or truncated abstracts, while the claims depend on numerical regions and plotted contours. Full-text passages, figure captions, and source assumptions must be quoted before treating these findings as established.

The synthesis mixes keV dark-matter production with MeV–GeV late-decaying HNL BBN constraints and with nonminimal production models. The final map must separate mass regime, abundance fraction, production mechanism, lifetime, and whether a point is a published joint constraint or an assembled conditional comparison.

open_directions_ranked.why: The current record establishes the qualitative exclusion structure but does not provide the numerical flavor-specific mass–mixing boundaries.
The surviving keV regions depend on correlated production and structure assumptions and cannot yet be represented by one quantitative joint map.
Both regions are conditionally viable, but their different lepton-asymmetry histories and structure criteria prevent a direct comparison.
The 2024–2025 literature shows that additional decay channels can substantially change BBN limits in the MeV–GeV regime.
These mechanisms can reopen parameter space, but their viability remains model-dependent and must be tested jointly against X-ray and structure constraints.
